newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, China to hold construction seminar.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, China to hold construction seminar.

text.p: A Taiwan delegation will travel to China for a seminar this weekend on forging closer links in the construction industry between the two diplmatic rivals, the trip's organiser said on Wednesday.
"The mainland market there is huge and we have to start understanding it before we enter," said Sun Kuang, secretary-general of Taiwan's Construction Management Association.

About 30 Taiwan construction-industry executives and university professors will swap views on the Taiwan and China construction markets with Chinese officials and representatives of mainland construction firms, Sun said.
The three-day seminar begins Saturday in Shanghai.
Taiwan's construction sector has been mired in recession since the real estate market peaked in 1989.
By contrast, China's nationwide construction boomed in the early 1990s but has cooled somewhat in the past three years due to a central-government clampdown on loose credit and risky investments.
Sun said the Taiwanese delegates and their Chinese counterparts would meet again in Shanghai after the seminar to explore joint business opportunities.

Taiwan has banned official contact with China since a civil war split them in 1949, but a political thaw begun in the late 1980s has engendered huge civilian business links between the longtime rivals.
